analysis: The PR change is test-only: it adds one Swift test, theDaemonStateReportsTheFilterACommittedSwitchApplied, in ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift at head lines 189-229. It is parameterized on accepted true/false. It uses MockCoordinator and a temp-directory config and state file. It checks that the daemon state.json reports enabled_models_at_start and enabled_models_at_last_switch after a committed switch. The last-switch value is nil when the commit is refused and rolled back. It also checks that the saved provider.toml ends with the new or old enabled_models accordingly. No production code is changed in the supplied units, so no trust-boundary behavior (TB-002 coordinator WebSocket, TB-007 inference engine, TB-011 authorization) is altered. No new attack surface, secrets, network endpoints, or privilege paths are introduced. The test uses a local mock coordinator on loopback, ephemeral temp directories removed via defer, and a fabricated public key string. It reveals no real credentials. The rest of the file (the other tests) is unchanged; I read it for context only and did not treat it as changed behavior. Remaining integration questions: the production code that writes enabled_models_at_last_switch into the daemon state is outside the supplied evidence. The test asserts a contract (a refused commit restores no filter and the config is rolled back) that is only as sound as that unseen implementation. Nothing here shows a security regression. The threat model's T-041 cache definition is not touched by this diff.
